idea-plugin.name: AI Unified Process Navigator
idea-plugin.description:
Navigate between @UseCase annotated test methods and their Markdown specs — and see a live activity diagram of the Use Case you are editing.

Live activity diagram

The AI Unified Process Diagram tool window renders a PlantUML activity diagram of the Use Case spec (UC-*.md, SUC-*.md, BUC-*.md) in the selected editor: the Main Success Scenario is the spine, every Alternative Flow branches at the step its trigger references. The diagram updates as you type and is rendered entirely in-process (MIT-licensed PlantUML with the Smetana engine) — no Graphviz, no external rendering service, the spec never leaves your IDE.

BPMN editor

*.bpmn process models open in the bpmn-js modeler of the AI Unified Process Studio — palette, canvas, and properties panel — with the XML still available in the Text tab. Both tabs edit the same document, so diagram edits are regular, undoable file changes. The editor runs in the IDE's embedded browser from files bundled with the plugin; nothing is loaded from the network. The toolbar exports the diagram as SVG or PNG, and ```bpmn fences show as diagrams in the Markdown preview.

Navigation between specs and tests

  • Gutter icon on @UseCase annotation jumps to the matching spec file (UC-XXX-*.md, SUC-XXX-*.md, BUC-XXX-*.md, each also with an optional project prefix like petclinic-UC-XXX-*.md)
  • Gutter icon on **Use Case ID:** UC-XXX in Markdown jumps to all test methods with that ID
  • Gutter icon on ### BR-XXX business rule headers jumps to tests referencing that rule
  • Find Usages (Alt+F7) works in both directions, and an inspection flags Use Case IDs without a spec

Tests may be written in Java or Kotlin — the annotation is read through UAST, so any JVM language the IDE supports works the same way.

Setup: the host project must define an annotation type called UseCase with attributes id, scenario, and businessRules. If the plugin sees Markdown specs in a project but no such annotation, it offers a one-time balloon with a "Create UseCase.java" action that scaffolds the file into a chosen source root.

Works with the AI Unified Process methodology.
